title: Greywater Bay Rising Anew
premise: Sable Coldharbour, the observant concierge of the Greywater Bay Grand Hotel, has spent decades making themselves unremarkable—until a drowned body washes up wearing clothes lifted from Sable's own closet, and the police fixate on them as either victim or killer. The dead man turns out to be connected to a thirty-year-old disappearance Sable witnessed as a child, one whose statute of limitations expires in six weeks. As Sable quietly investigates the hotel's long-serving staff and guests, they uncover a found family of misfits who have been protecting each other's secrets for decades, forcing Sable to choose between legal justice and a mercy the law cannot offer. In the end, Sable exposes the true killer—the hotel's beloved former manager—and lets the aging accomplices walk free, finally claiming a name, a family, and a place in Greywater Bay.
about_author: Freya Sandoval is a former night-shift desk clerk who spent eleven years in coastal hotels collecting the stories guests thought no one overheard. She writes mysteries about invisible people who see everything, from a houseboat moored somewhere off the Pacific Northwest.

chapters.title: The Uniform of the Dead
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A routine foggy morning at the Grand Hotel shatters when police arrive: a body pulled from the bay is dressed in Sable's own missing clothes. Detective Imara Voss treats Sable as suspect, not witness. Emotional beat: the terror of being seen after a lifetime of careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Interrogated, Sable deflects with practiced blandness but privately recognizes the dead man: Tomas Reyes, a bellhop who vanished in 1994, the year eight-year-old Sable saw something in the hotel's flooded sub-basement. Emotional beat: dread resurfacing like something long submerged.

chapters.title: The Registry Nobody Reads
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with a flashback chapter-within. Digging through old ledgers, Sable reconstructs the summer of 1994: Reyes's last shift, an argument overheard through a laundry chute, and a guest registry page torn out. Emotional beat: the child's-eye confusion of witnessing without understanding.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven in Wool
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and Voss POV. Voss pulls employment records; three current staff members—housekeeper Marisol, engineer Dev, and retired doorman Ambrose—all claim Reyes simply quit. Their stories align too perfectly. Emotional beat: Sable realizing the people who raised them may be lying in chorus.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A second body surfaces: the retired coroner who signed Reyes's original death certificate, drowned in her bathtub with a hotel keycard nearby. The statute clock ticks louder. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve—someone is silencing witnesses, and Sable is next.

chapters.title: The Family We Chose
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol confronts Sable, revealing fragments: Reyes discovered the manager, Edmund Hale, was embezzling and worse, and the staff covered it up to protect each other—not to protect Hale. Emotional beat: the fierce, compromised love of a found family bound by shared guilt.

chapters.title: Six Weeks to Midnight
chapters.summary: Sable and Voss POV alternating. Voss admits off-record she suspects the old case was buried; Sable realizes helping her means betraying the only family they've had. Dev's workshop is ransacked; a threatening note uses Sable's childhood nickname, known to very few. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling against conscience.

chapters.title: The Sub-Basement Speaks
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable returns to the flooded sub-basement and finds what the child saw: not a murder, but Reyes alive, hiding, and Hale finding him first. A hidden ledger proves Hale killed Reyes and framed the cover-up so the staff would be complicit forever. Emotional beat: the past reassembling into terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, climax. Hale, now dying and still revered, corners Sable in the penthouse, offering absolution and silence. Sable records his confession as Voss arrives; Hale collapses mid-threat, and the truth spills publicly before he can be charged. Emotional beat: fury, pity, and the hollow taste of justice that arrives too late for the law.

chapters.title: Greywater Bay Rising Anew
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the hotel reopens under new management—Marisol, Dev, and Ambrose at Sable's side. Voss closes the file unofficially; the surviving staff keep their freedom and their shame. Sable signs their full name in the new registry for the first time. Emotional beat: quiet belonging, earned rather than inherited.
